name: AR-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deep-red district with R+23 partisan lean
Incumbent Rick Crawford renominated with large financial advantage
Democrat Terri Green raised only $65k with $12k on hand
Prediction markets give Democrats about a 1% chance
model.rationale: The baseline of R+19.5 rests on a strong R+23 lean, a well-funded incumbent, and a severely underfunded challenger, with no polls or expert ratings suggesting movement. Prediction markets at 1% for Democrats confirm Safe R, so I hold essentially at the baseline.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge for Green or an unexpected Crawford scandal could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains highly unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arkansas's 1st District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of R+23. Incumbent Rick Crawford was renominated and enters the general election with a commanding financial position: nearly $950,000 raised and over $1 million on hand. His Democratic opponent, Terri Green, has raised only about $65,000 and had under $12,000 in cash, leaving her little capacity to communicate with voters. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot but is not a significant factor.

There are no public polls of the race and no expert raters have flagged it as competitive, so the forecast rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets put Democratic chances at roughly 1%. With a strong incumbent, a heavily favorable district, and a large resource gap, this race is rated Safe Republican with a margin near twenty points.
